newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand ended weak against the dollar on Thursday but was off the day's worst levels on central Reserve Bank action after the local unit slid to within a whisker of its record low in the morning, dealers said.
Bonds softened to their worst levels in two months, but short-covering during the afternoon gave the market a small boost.

The rand finished at 4.5840/90 on the dollar from 4.5685/5735 at 1400 GMT on Wednesday after the unit earlier slid to a two-month low of 4.5865 bid after local banks rushed in to buy dollars amid overnight bond market weakness.
Foreigners were seen taking up dollars in the market during the afternoon.
"The Reserve Bank was pretty determined today," said a dealer.
"It it wasn't for the bank it (the rand) would probably have got to 4.59," the dealer said referring to the unit's record low touched on August 19.
Dealers said it was likely the Bank had left sizeable orders with banks to prevent the rand from sliding further in after-hours trade when it left the market.
They said the rand was likely to breach the 4.59 level on the upside in the next few days, possibly as early as Friday.
"It will get to 4.59 in the next few days. The only thing that was holding it from there today is the Reserve Bank. But they won't be able to hold it forever," one said.

Against the crosses, the rand fell to fresh lows against the British pound touching a worst level of bid in early dealings. It later recovered slightly to last trade at 7.2888/2991 from 7.2984/3110 late Wednesday. On the mark, the rand was at 0.3320/3325 from 0.3353/3357 previously.
On the bond market the key R150 long bond was at 15.635 pct from 15.44 at 1400 GMT Wednesday after it slumped to a worst level of 15.67 bid.

Dealers said late short-covering helped bonds off their weakest levels after foreigners had earlier sold stock amid a delayed reaction to a worse-than-expected September inflation data released on Wednesday.
"There has been a little bit of demand as local players covered their short positions. There was also some options-related stuff," a dealer said.
Traders said the market could regain some composure on Friday ahead of fairly upbeat forecasts on September M3 money supply due for release during the day.
"We could get down to between 15.58 and 15.52 percent as money supply is expected to be quite good," a dealer said.
However, further weakness on the rand on Friday would cap gains, with the market also technically weak, they said.
"Technically 15.65 percent is a key level. If it breaks that again it could run up to 15.74."

Economists forecast M3 would grow at a slower rate of 15.1 percent in September compared with a preliminary 15.51 percent in August. Private sector credit extension was expected to ease to 17.3 from 17.71 percent in August.
September trade data, also due on Friday, drew a consensus forecast of a 720 million rand surplus compared with a 130 million rand surplus in August.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners bought a net 244.71 million ranth African bonds on Wednesday after buying 36.29 million rand the previous day.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 3.76 billion rand from 3.93 billion rand on Tuesday.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 16.15 percent bid and 16 percent. The 90-day BA rate was unchanged at between 15.55 and 15.40 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage slightly higher at 7.887 billion rand on Wednesday from 7.629 billion rand on Tuesday.
-- Nicole Mordant, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
